rules.rationale: High-dose nitroglycerin is considered a safe and effective treatment option for patients with acute heart failure syndrome and elevated blood pressure.
rules.citation: Section 3, Level C recommendation.

rules.rationale: High dose nitroglycerin can be administered as an infusion starting at 0.3 to 0.5 mcg/kg per minute, increased in increments of 20 mcg/min every 1 to 3 minutes.
rules.citation: Section 3, Levy et al study description.

rules.rationale: High dose nitroglycerin can be administered as bolus intravenous dosing of 2,000 mcg every 3 to 5 minutes.
rules.citation: Section 3, Levy et al study description.

rules.rationale: Bolus dosing of nitroglycerin is 2,000 mcg every 3 to 5 minutes.
rules.citation: Section 3, Levy et al study description.

rules.rationale: Infusion dose starts at 0.3 to 0.5 mcg/kg per minute, increased in increments of 20 mcg/min every 1 to 3 minutes.
rules.citation: Section 3, Levy et al study description.

rules.rationale: If systolic blood pressure falls below 90 mm Hg, further increased dosage of nitroglycerin should be discontinued.
rules.citation: Section 3, Levy et al study description.

rules.rationale: Maximum potential bolus dose of nitroglycerin is 20 mg (20,000 mcg).
rules.citation: Section 3, Levy et al study description.

rules.rationale: Maximum infusion dose of nitroglycerin is 400 mcg/min.
rules.citation: Section 3, Levy et al study description.

rules.rationale: High-dose nitroglycerin therapy in acute heart failure syndrome trended toward reducing the need for endotracheal intubation within 6 hours.
rules.citation: The patients receiving high-dose nitroglycerin showed a trend toward improvement in the primary efficacy endpoint of reduced endotracheal intubations within 6 hours (13.8% [95% CI 4.8% to 29.5%] versus 26.7% [95% CI, 15.5% to 40.8%]).
rules.citation_verbatim_excerpt: The patients receiving high-dose nitroglycerin showed a trend toward improvement in the primary efficacy endpoint of reduced endotracheal intubations within 6 hours (13.8% [95% CI 4.8% to 29.5%] versus 26.7% [95% CI, 15.5% to 40.8%]).

rules.rationale: High-flow oxygen with a 100% nonrebreather mask was part of the initial guideline-recommended therapy administered to AHFS patients in respiratory distress, alongside sublingual nitroglycerin and furosemide.
rules.citation: Initial therapy consisted of Class I recommendations from the American Heart Association's 2000 “Guidelines for the Evaluation and Management of Heart Failure,” including high-flow oxygen, with 100% nonrebreather mask, sublingual nitroglycerin 400 mcg every 5 minutes up to a maximum of 4 treatments, and furosemide 60 to 80 mg intravenously.
